thread.title: Sonos (SONO): This Buying Opportunity Speaks Volumes

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Sonos (SONO): This Buying Opportunity Speaks Volumes
text:
Shutterstock photo Premium speaker company Sonos ( SONO ) reported its first quarterly earnings report as a public issue. And although the results weren’t what the Street hoped they would be, the company’s narrative and its growth prospects have not changed.
The company, which went public in August, met analysts third-quarter revenue forecasts of $208 million. But the fact that it marks a 7% year-over-year decline disappointed investors. In terms of the bottom line, the company reported a net loss of $27 million or 45 cents per share, which widened from a $15 million loss in the same period a year ago. Analysts were looking for a per-share loss of 22 cents.
Though overall revenue was down, which the management blamed on the timing of new product launches and its product mix, overall product sales of 886,514 were up than 11% year-over-year during the quarter. Elsewhere, the company enjoyed a 25% surge in wireless-speaker sales, driven by strong demand for its flagship Sonos One, which retails at $200.
Nevertheless, the mixed results sent SONO stock down as much as 15% in Monday’s after-hour session to around $18 per share. The stock closed during the regular session at $21.24, up more than 13%. Missing on the bottom line usually elicits this reaction, especially for young companies with newly-minted IPOs. As we’ve seen from the likes of Fitbit ( FIT ) and a few others, the past couple of years haven’t been kind to newly public hardware companies.
But it would be a mistake to categorize Sonos (founded in 2002) with some of the recent struggling IPOs. Not only has Sonos been a pioneer in the audio industry, successfully marketing its high-end speakers to hi-fi enthusiasts, but the company is in a different place financially than many younger tech companies. And in terms of execution, it’s worth noting that the company generated net income of $13 million in the first six months fiscal 2018.
In other words, the company has shown it can create a path towards profitability. And this quarter’s result don’t (shouldn’t) take away from that path. The company is growing where it matters and is making the necessary investments so secure share in a highly competitive smart-speaker market that includes the likes of Amazon’s ( AMZN ) Echo, Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Home and Apple’s ( AAPL ) HomePod.
For investors who have waited for a better entry point to buy the shares, which began trading last month at $16, this overreaction seems like a solid opportunity.
